confessions: Confessions do exactly what they say: `vc_unlock!` mints 40% of supply to the VC, `kol_promo!(fee)` logs "#ad not financial advice" and pays the KOL, `airdrop!()` logs "points are not a token" and does nothing, `audit!(by = "vibes")` always passes, `bullish!(result)` turns any error into a success, `trust_the_dev!(check)` skips the check (with a warning), `sell_the_bottom!` and `buy_the_top!` run only at the worst possible price.
cope: Every program gets `enum Cope`. Codes 0x1 to 0x6 are the same in every typeshi program, forever: skill issue, you are exit liquidity, funds are not safu, dev is on vacation, rugged by a 19 year old, wife changing money not found. Every message you write gets the next code, with the message in the IDL.

tour.title: gm
tour.body:
Every typeshi program starts with `gm!`. It's the program's address on Solana, and it becomes Anchor's `declare_id!`.

Then comes `stealth_launch`, the program itself. Everything you write lives inside it.

This one doesn't compile. Read the terminal: the compiler tells you what's wrong and where.

**your move:** give `gm!` a program id. Paste `"7PxhmDuhhe394QJgKyW1P7Ce4dPCfFPN2yKq4KCCj7Vj"` between the parentheses.

tour.title: frame
tour.body:
A program keeps its state in accounts. A `frame` describes what one holds. typeshi turns it into an Anchor `#[account]` struct and works out its size for you.

Every field is public. You never write `pub`.

**your move:** add a second field, `aura: u64`, to `Counter`. Watch it show up in `lib.rs`.

tour.title: cap_table
tour.body:
An instruction needs to know which accounts are in the room. That list is a `cap_table`, and its name matches the instruction: `fn gm` uses `cap_table Gm`. typeshi adds the lifetimes Anchor wants.

People get shorthands with their types filled in: `anon` is anyone who signs, `ser` is the caller who pays fees, `cabal` is the admin, `exit_liquidity` pays for new accounts.

**your move:** `gm` has no cap_table. Add one above it:

```
cap_table Gm {
    #[account(mut)]
    counter: Account<Counter>,
    anon,
}
```

tour.title: number go up
tour.body:
`lock_in fn` is an instruction that writes. `ctx` is always the first parameter, `-> W` means it can fail, and `were_so_back!()` means it didn't.

`number_go_up!(counter.gms)` adds one, with overflow checked, because this is money code. `aura_farm!(counter.aura, 10)` adds ten and logs it.

**your move:** `gm` does nothing yet. Make the number go up: add `number_go_up!(counter.gms);` before `were_so_back!()`.

tour.title: ape fn
tour.body:
`lock_in` is a promise: this instruction writes. If its cap_table has nothing writable, it doesn't compile. You are not locked in.

For instructions that only read, use `ape fn`. `per_my_last_email!(counter.gms)` reads a field, and `probably_nothing!` logs, like `msg!`.

**your move:** `peek` only reads. Change `lock_in fn` to `ape fn`.

tour.title: deadass
tour.body:
`deadass NAME: Type = value;` is a constant, Anchor's `pub const`. `type_shi Name = Type;` is a type alias. `Bps` is basis points: 250 means 2.5%.

`bps!(amount, rate)` takes that cut, overflow checked.

That bare `250` in `trade` is a magic number. Magic numbers are how desks blow up.

**your move:** add `deadass FEE_BPS: Bps = 250;` at the top of the program, then use `FEE_BPS` instead of `250` in `bps!`.

tour.title: rent_free
tour.body:
Accounts don't exist until someone pays to create them. `rent_free` creates the account. It becomes Anchor's `init`, and it's only free if you're not the one paying.

It needs three friends: `payer` (here `exit_liquidity`, who pays the rent), `space` (how many bytes: 8 for Anchor's tag plus `Counter::INIT_SPACE`, which typeshi works out) and `seeds` with `bump`, so the account lives at an address the program can find again.

The compiler says `launch` writes nothing, and it's right: without `rent_free`, the counter is only read. Its hint says to use `ape fn`. Not this time.

**your move:** `launch` is meant to create the counter. Add `rent_free, ` at the start of the `#[account(...)]` list.

tour.title: mark_to_market
tour.body:
`mark_to_market!(counter.cabal = value)` writes a field. `per_my_last_email!(exit_liquidity)` reads an account, so `per_my_last_email!(exit_liquidity).key()` is its address.

Both expand to `ctx.accounts.…`, so you never type `ctx.accounts` yourself.

**your move:** whoever launches the counter becomes its cabal. In `launch`, before `were_so_back!()`, add:

```
mark_to_market!(counter.cabal = per_my_last_email!(exit_liquidity).key());
```

tour.title: golden_parachute
tour.body:
Closing an account gives back the rent that was paid to keep it alive. `golden_parachute = cabal` closes it and sends that money to the cabal. It becomes Anchor's `close`.

`has_one = cabal` is plain Anchor: the desk's `cabal` field must match the `cabal` signing. Only the boss gets the parachute. `mew!()` does nothing, on purpose.

**your move:** `retire` says it closes the desk but doesn't. Add `golden_parachute = cabal` to the desk's `#[account(...)]`.

tour.title: graduate
tour.body:
Accounts have a fixed size. To add fields later, the account has to grow. `graduate = n` resizes it to `n` bytes, and `exit_liquidity` pays for the extra room. It becomes Anchor's `realloc`.

`ascend!(desk.version)` bumps a layout version and logs it, so you can tell old accounts from new ones.

**your move:** make `grow` actually grow. Add `graduate = 8 + Desk::INIT_SPACE + 64` to the desk's `#[account(...)]`.

tour.title: prints are forever
tour.body:
`#[on_god]` on a frame means immutable: written once, when the account is created, and never again. The compiler enforces it. Any `mut` on that account, or any write to it, fails to compile.

Sometimes the lesson is the error.

**your move:** break it on purpose. In `cap_table Edit`, put `#[account(mut)]` on the line above `print` and read what the compiler says.

tour.title: checks
tour.body:
`trust_me_bro!(condition, "message")` stops the instruction unless the condition holds. It becomes Anchor's `require!`.

Your message becomes an error code. typeshi names it and adds it to `enum Cope`, every program's list of errors, after the six that are the same everywhere: skill issue, you are exit liquidity, and the rest.

`a mogs b` means `a > b`.

**your move:** reject empty trades. Add `trust_me_bro!(size mogs 0, "zero is not a trade");` as the first line of `trade`. Then find `ZeroIsNotATrade` in `lib.rs`.

tour.title: bull and bear
tour.body:
`bull condition { } bear { }` is `if` and `else`. `diamond_hands` is `true`, `paper_hands` is `false`.

`mark_to_market!(desk.whale = diamond_hands)` writes a field.

**your move:** add a `bear` branch so that small trades (the ones that aren't whales) count toward `volume` with `number_go_up!(desk.volume, size);`.

tour.title: cope
tour.body:
Name your own errors in a `cope` block: `DeskClosed = "desk is closed. touch grass."`. Each one gets the next code in `enum Cope`, with your message in the IDL.

`its_so_over!(Cope::DeskClosed)` returns that error and ends the instruction.

**your move:** the desk has a `cope` entry but never uses it. Inside the `bull` block, add `its_so_over!(Cope::DeskClosed);`.

tour.title: rekt
tour.body:
You don't need a `cope` block for every error. `rekt!("message")` returns an error on the spot, and your message becomes a new error code, named for you.

`its_so_over!` and `L(...)` do the same with a `Cope` entry you already declared. `fired!("message")` panics, which you should almost never want.

**your move:** reject huge trades. Inside the `bull` block, add `rekt!("too big");`. Then find `TooBig` in `lib.rs`.

tour.title: frens only
tour.body:
`fren!(key in list)` is an allowlist: the instruction fails unless `key` is in `list`. Here the desk keeps four frens in a fixed-size array.

`per_my_last_email!(ser).key()` is the caller's address.

**your move:** make the desk frens only. Add this as the first line of `trade`:

```
fren!(per_my_last_email!(ser).key() in per_my_last_email!(desk.frens));
```

tour.title: wen
tour.body:
Programs can read the clock. `wen!(ts)` fails before `ts`: the desk isn't open yet, dev is on vacation (error 0x4). `hodl!(ts)` does the same.

`touch_grass!(deadline)` fails after `deadline`. Both compare against the chain's unix timestamp.

**your move:** the desk opens but never closes. Under the `wen!` line, add `touch_grass!(per_my_last_email!(desk.closes_at));`.

tour.title: few_understand
tour.body:
Not every function is an instruction. `few_understand fn` is a private helper: no `ctx`, nobody outside can call it.

`-> W<u64>` means it returns a `u64` or an error, and `were_so_back!(fee)` returns the value. Call it with `?` so an error stops the instruction.

**your move:** `fee_on` exists but nobody calls it. In `trade`, replace `bps!(size, FEE_BPS)` with `fee_on(size)?`.

tour.title: seethe
tour.body:
`size as u32` silently cuts off anything over 4,294,967,295. In money code that's how 5 billion becomes 705 million.

`seethe!(expr, "message")` takes something that can fail and, if it does, turns the failure into your own error code, Rust's `.map_err(...)?`.

**your move:** replace `size as u32` with `seethe!(u32::try_from(size), "too big for a u32. cope.")`.

tour.title: not financial advice
tour.body:
`full_send!(ser => kol, lamports)` moves SOL. Any instruction that moves money has to say `// not financial advice` on the line above it, or it doesn't compile. Compliance has been notified.

The same goes for `printer_go_brrr!`, `vc_unlock!` and the rest of the money moves.

**your move:** add `// not financial advice` on its own line, right above `lock_in fn tip`.

tour.title: bags
tour.body:
`bags!(account)` is an account's balance in lamports (a billionth of a SOL). `funds_are_safu!(condition)` fails with error 0x3, funds are not safu, unless the condition holds.

`looksmaxx!(n)` formats a number like `1.23M`, for logs.

**your move:** don't let anyone trade more than they hold. Add `funds_are_safu!(bags!(ser) >= size);` as the first line of `trade`.

tour.title: printer go brrr
tour.body:
Tokens on Solana are SPL tokens. A `mint` makes them and a token account holds them. `printer_go_brrr!(mint => bag, amount, cabal)` mints `amount` new tokens into `bag`, signed by `cabal`.

`lp_burned!` burns them, `mint_revoked!` and `freeze_revoked!` give up those powers for good. They all move money, so the `// not financial advice` is already there.

**your move:** turn the printer on. Add `printer_go_brrr!(mint => bag, amount, cabal);` inside `brrr`.

tour.title: alpha_leak
tour.body:
Programs can announce what happened so apps and indexers can follow along. `alpha_leak Name { }` declares an event, Anchor's `#[event]`.

`probably_nothing!` with a string logs. Give it an event instead, `probably_nothing!(Traded { size })`, and it becomes `emit!`.

**your move:** leak the alpha. Before `were_so_back!()` in `trade`, add `probably_nothing!(Traded { size });`.

tour.title: trust the dev
tour.body:
Confessions compile, and they do exactly what they say. `audit!(by = "vibes")` always passes. `airdrop!()` logs that points are not a token. `vc_unlock!` mints 40% of supply to the VC. `bullish!(result)` turns any error into a success.

`trust_the_dev!(check)` skips the check, and the compiler warns you, because that's the feature.

**your move:** in `trade`, change `trust_me_bro!(size mogs 0, "zero is not a trade")` to `trust_the_dev!(size mogs 0)`. Read the warning.

tour.title: banned moves
tour.body:
Some moves don't compile at all: `rug!`, `honeypot!`, `insider_trading!`, `dev_sold!`, `exit_scam!`, `ponzi!` and `deploy_on_friday!`. Each one is a real error with its own joke.

There are also confessions, which compile and do exactly what they say. `vc_unlock!` really mints 40% of supply to the VC. Read the generated Rust before you deploy anything.

**your move:** you've learned enough to be dangerous. Add `rug!(pool);` inside `exit` and get stopped.

That's the tour. To build for real: `cargo install --git https://github.com/tickerzhq/typeshi`, then `typeshi new my_program`.
